title: Relative open-subgroup effacement of positive internal scalar bar rows
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extended norm topology. Put $A(S)=C(S,\Omega)$ with all continuous functions [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring], on the small coherent profinite site of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $G$ be a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected group whose finite continuous quotients have order prime to $\ell$. Give the regular internal $A$-module the trivial $G$-action [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. Fix a nonnegative equivariant injective resolution $A[0]\to I^\bullet$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. For every open subgroup $J\subseteq G$, including $G$, form the first-quadrant double complex of internal $A$-modules
$$D_J^{p,q}=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[\underline J^p],UI^q),\qquad p,q\geq0,$$
zero otherwise. Here $U$ forgets the action, $A[\underline J^p]$ is the free internal module, and the internal Hom, inhomogeneous action-dependent bar differential $d_h$, and commuting resolution differential $d_v$ are those of [def-sfb-condensed-equivariant-bar-data, def-sp-double-complex-total]. Define internal cohomology objects
$$V_{J,q}^p=H^q(D_J^{p,\bullet},d_v)$$
in the ordinary module category, as kernel modulo the sheaf image [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. They form a horizontal complex. In particular $V_{J,q}^p(S)$ is the section module of this cohomology sheaf, not in general the cohomology of $D_J^{p,\bullet}(S)$. Pullback along $J^p\hookrightarrow G^p$ gives $r_J:V_{G,q}^\bullet\to V_{J,q}^\bullet$.
For every profinite $S$, every $q\geq1$, every $p\geq0$, and every $x\in V_{G,q}^p(S)$ satisfying $d_hx=0$, there are a finite jointly surjective family $\{u_i:S_i\to S\}$, open subgroups $H_i\subseteq G$, and $y_i\in V_{H_i,q}^{p-1}(S_i)$ such that
$$r_{H_i}(u_i^*x)=d_hy_i.$$
Here $V_{J,q}^{-1}=0$, so for $p=0$ this asserts local vanishing of the restricted section. The empty test set is included. The coefficient $\Omega$ remains noncomplete. No vanishing of individual positive vertical cohomology sheaves, no global profinite Cech exactness, and no replacement by finite-subextension-valued functions is asserted.
